Date: Thu, 06 Nov 2025 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity: occupancy & session-span snapshot for Orbit9

Hi Sanjay / Elena,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — great product fit. To get a realistic dedicated-capacity estimate that we can present to your finance and infra teams, can you send a short traffic snapshot with the fields below? A CSV export is ideal (you can attach). If anything below isn’t available, mark as N/A and call out any assumptions.

Requested fields / notes:
- Observation window: 7 days (UTC) if possible — date range you supply
- Per-minute request counts (timestamped) and per-request token counts (prompt tokens, response tokens)
- Session identifier + session start/end timestamps (so we can compute session span distribution)
- Peak concurrency observed by minute (p50, p90, p99)
- Token-per-request distribution (histogram bins or raw percentiles)
- Percent of responses > 512 tokens and > 1024 tokens
- Synchronous vs async/queued endpoints (which endpoints are batch processed?)
- Typical prompt categories (search, chat-assistant, summarization, rerank) and approximate % mix
- Expected dayparting (regional/local peak hours) and geo split (us/eu/apac)
- Any KV-cache reuse hints (average prefix-cache hit rate; if you do session-level caching, an estimate is fine)
- SLA/latency target for the endpoints (p50/p95/p99) and acceptable degradation policy for a canary/fallback

Deliverable: a CSV plus a one-paragraph context note (what changes in the 7-day window, any spikes related to batch jobs, special events).

We aim to turn this into a first-pass sizing (GPU mix + reserved counts + buffer/burst plan) within 48 hours of receiving the sample. Can you confirm whether you can share the CSV by EOD PT tomorrow? Also copying procurement — let us know if we should attach an NDA.

Thanks,
Chloe

Chloe — thanks, we can do that. Attached is a 7-day export (sample truncated) with minute-level counts, session IDs, and token fields. Quick highlights from our side so you don’t have to wait on parsing: 

- Avg concurrent sessions (global): 1,150 (weekday baseline)
- Observed peak concurrent sessions (5-min window): 3,820 (p99 spike during product launch test)
- Average tokens/request: prompt 220 / response 360
- % responses >512 tokens: ~6% ; >1024 tokens: ~1.1%
- Session span: median 18s; p90 ~2.7 minutes; long-tail: p99 ~24 minutes (interactive sessions)
- Endpoint mix: 72% chat-assistant (sync), 18% summarization (async batch), 10% rerank/embeddings (mixed)
- KV-cache: we don’t have a full prefix cache implemented yet; estimated session-level reuse ~12%
- Geo split: US 64% / EU 22% / APAC 14%
- Latency targets: chat p95 < 350ms, summarization batch SLA p95 within 3s (we’re comfortable with longer tail for batch)

We attached: orbit9_traffic_sample.csv (CSV, 42 KB) — it’s redacted for PII. If you need raw logs we can work with security to provide a sanitized extract.

Sanjay

Thanks Sanjay — very helpful. A few clarifying items before our sizing pass: 

1) For the long-tail sessions (p99 ~24 min) — are those true sustained model usage (active token generation across the duration) or idle sessions that re-use cached context intermittently? That matters for KV cache and memory residency.

2) For the 6% >512 tokens bucket — are those concentrated on a single endpoint or distributed across chat + summarization?

3) Can you confirm the summarization jobs are scheduled outside peak hours (e.g., nightly batch windows) or do they sometimes overlap with chat spikes?

I’ve looped in Karthik for recommended GPU mix and Vivek for migration/rollout planning (multi-site placements and replication). Karthik — high level ask: based on the attached sample and the geo split, can you provide a quick first-pass reserved capacity sketch (GPU types, counts, recommended concurrency per GPU, and recommended buffer/burst margin)? We’ll then iterate and map to pricing. 

If convenient, we can do a 30-min sizing call tomorrow morning PT. Sanjay/Elena — does 9:00am PT on Monday, Nov 10 work?

-Chloe

Thanks for the sample — I took a quick pass and sketched a conservative first-pass reserved capacity plan. Notes and assumptions are inline.

Assumptions (from sample):
- Sustained baseline concurrency: 1,150 (weekday), peak short windows up to 3,820 (p99)
- Average token mix: prompt 220 / response 360 with 6% >512 tokens
- Chat endpoints are latency-sensitive (p95 <350ms) and require GPU-backed real-time inference
- Summarization largely batch; assume 60-80% of summarization can be scheduled outside peak with small burst windows

First-pass recommendation (reserved + burst):
- GPU mix: target H100-80GB for chat nodes (primary) + A100-80GB for overflow/batch and mixed workloads. H100 yields better throughput on longer responses and quantized models; A100 is cost-effective for bursty batch tasks.
- Reserved baseline (sustained): 6 x H100-80GB (each conservatively sized for ~600 concurrent low-latency chat connections with KV cache disabled and moderate batching). This maps to ~3,600 effective concurrent capacity at p50 with headroom for p90.
- Buffer/burst pool (reserved or on-demand depending on procurement appetite): 2–3 x A100-80GB for overflow and scheduled batch work (handles summarization and 6% larger responses without impacting chat SLOs).
- Safety spare for failover / upgrades: +1 H100 (hot standby) in the us-primary region

Why these numbers: with your p99 spike at ~3.8k, a 6x H100 reserved baseline covers sustained traffic plus a modest buffer; the A100 pool absorbs large response generation and scheduled summarization. If you adopt aggressive KV caching and batching (we can recommend config changes), you can drop the baseline by ~15–25%.

Concurrency per GPU (rough): H100-80GB -> 600 concurrent chat sessions (conservative, low-batch); A100-80GB -> 300–350 effective concurrent chat + batch mix.

Action items:
- Chloe: confirm whether long-tail sessions are active generation (Sanjay) or idle touches — if active, we’ll increase memory residency assumptions and likely +1–2 GPUs to baseline.
- Orbit9: can you share a short list of model variants in use (LLM family / sizes)? We can map quantized variants and recommended token limits per GPU.
- Commercial: Marissa — will map this to an ARR/commitment tier with a 12-month reserved pricing illustration.

I’ve attached a short playbook (redwood_sizing_playbook_v1.pdf) with our calculation worksheet and notes. Happy to jump on the 30-min call Monday to run through the math.

—Karthik
